date: # --- 2026-09-28, the attention-arm cost, measured AFTER 8fa5d4c ---------------
# The single most load-bearing row set in this file, and it is LATE: every
# earlier row was measured while the KDA arm returned a LEAF and trained
# nothing (AGENTS.md 3.2), so any step-time number that included "attention"
# was pricing a program that skipped the backward.
# All three below: small preset, 9,195,854 params, depth 2, seq 512, fp32,
# aux off, --no-engram, real_sharded corpus, dev profile (our crates at
# opt-level 0, no LTO), 25 steps timed, 3 concurrent compilers on the box.
# DEV PROFILE IS A CAVEAT, not a detail: it is the same for all three rows so
# the RATIO holds, but the absolute ms is not comparable to the release rows
# above. Do not mix them in one column.
# The three rows read together, and the third is the one that matters:
#   - removing the arm:            3076 ms
#   - adding the arm CORRECTLY:   25858 ms   -> the arm costs 22782 ms, 8.4x
#   - adding the arm with a leaf:   3098 ms   -> it appeared to cost 22 ms
# That third row is the whole trap. A fused forward that returns a leaf does no
# backward work, so it measured as ~1000x cheaper than the same arm computing
# what it is supposed to compute. Any speedup attributed to it in the project's
# history is measuring the absence of work.
# 158 tok/s at batch 8 x 512. 60k steps = 18 days, so a chunked recurrence
# built from ~4800 individual burn tensor ops does not train on this box and
# the fused adjoint is not an optimisation here, it is the difference between
# training and not training. See docs/AB-PROTOCOL.md for the queue this
# invalidates and AGENTS.md 3.3 for why the per-arm cost is currently unknown.
# NOT COMMITTED AS A BENCH: no repeat run, no release build, three compilers
# sharing the box, and the third row is from a different binary. Re-take
# before quoting any of it in an A/B budget.
# The VRAM rows correct a wrong claim rather than adding one. AGENTS.md and
# several docs said "batch 4 OOMs on 16 GB", which is true ONLY for the
# configuration with the JEPA teacher on (a second full forward). With aux off
# the card reaches batch 16 in 5908 MiB - 37% of 16 GB - so the earlier
# "we are pinned to batch 2" conclusion, which I repeated to the owner, was
# wrong. Throughput is flat from batch 8 to 16 (2.66 -> 2.99 KB/s), which is
# consistent with the workload being launch-bound rather than batch-bound:
# a bigger batch does not buy speed here, it buys a better gradient.
